drafts.neutral_framing: Should Brevard County’s lagoon program fund a living-filter pilot every year at a city stormwater outfall, with water tests before and after?
drafts.final_wording: Should the county’s lagoon program fund one living-filter pilot a year — an oyster reef, a living shoreline, or a nitrogen-removing filter bed — at a city stormwater outfall, and publish the water tests before and after?
drafts.final_wording_note: Framed around how the program spends money it already has. It does not ask about the November 3 lagoon tax renewal, which is an active ballot measure.
shaping_notes: A question about a method, not about any person, candidate, or ballot measure. The sales-tax renewal is deliberately left out; this question stands whether it passes or not.
Grounded in the county’s own BAM filter results and Brevard Zoo’s oyster reefs.

drafts.background: Storm drains in Brevard cities empty toward the Indian River Lagoon. Nitrogen and phosphorus washing off streets feed the algae blooms that killed the lagoon’s seagrass and, from 2020 to 2022, starved 1,255 manatees. The county’s lagoon program already builds BAM filters; one at Broadway Pond removes about 456 pounds of nitrogen a year. See Our water.

drafts.background: The Brevard County jail holds over 1,600 people a day; in February 2023, 86.8% had not been convicted. The Sheriff asked for $61.5 million to run it in FY2025-26. drafts.background: Brevard County posts line-item budget spreadsheets for its departments (32 department spreadsheets are posted). None were found for the Sheriff, Clerk, Tax Collector, Property Appraiser or Supervisor of Elections. The elected officers’ budgets — $258.4 million, $220.4 million of it the Sheriff — appear in the county’s budget book, but not in the downloadable line-item spreadsheets. Not posted means not found yet, not hidden.
